newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses make poor start on rates worry.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses make poor start on rates worry.

text.p: European stocks made a poor start to the week on Monday as uncertainty over interest rates outweighed optimism engendered by Wall Street's third consecutive record close on Friday.
On currency markets, the dollar, which fell last week, was slightly weaker in early transactions with traders seeing little in U.S. economic data due this week to ignite a take-off.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, shares slipped 0.3 percent. Traders said the market, already well below October's record levels, could come under more pressure from worries about rising interest rates.
"London is painting itself into a corner with these worries about domestic interest rates," said one.

Investors, already unsettled by a surprise quarter-point rate rise earlier this month, were further rattled by a Bank of England warning last week that inflation could breach the government's official target.
London stocks fell further after Monday's figures showing British producer input prices rose 0.5 percent in October, fuelled by a sharp rise in oil prices.
"I think we will get further downside," said one analyst. "There could be a further interest rate rise and rising rates are normally death for equities."
Others called the jitters over interest rates and inflation overdone. They saw the market mood improving once it was clear that 1997 would offer better growth with continued low inflation.
"The rating on the market is not terribly demanding and I don't see the need to be so worried," one trader said. "Not all interest rate increases are bad for equities."
In Frankfurt, stocks were down at the start, not drawing much comfort from the Dow Jones industrial average which closed at 6,219.82 points on Friday, the third peak in as many days.
The Dax index, which itself closed at a record high of 2,739.83 on Friday, slipped in thin trading, with the weaker dollar depressing the market.
The Paris bourse was closed for a national holiday commemorating the end of World War One.
The dollar slipped against the yen and mark in early European transactions with little respite expected from U.S. data this week, analysts said.

Many dealers will be awaiting the rate-setting meeting of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Wednesday and U.S. retail sales and consumer prices on Thursday for clues on the health of the American economy.

"We expect the (U.S.) economic data to undershoot and there is near universal agreement that the FOMC is not going to raise rates," said Klaus Baader, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5042 marks and 111.44 yen, compared with 1.5045 marks and 111.60 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 8.8 points lower at 3,902.0.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 4.13 points at at 2,735.70.
The Paris bourse was closed for the day.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1030 GMT
Gold was quoted at $379.90 an ounce in early European trade, versus $378.95 at the London close on Friday. Silver firmed to $4.86 from $4.81 on Friday.
